gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Creality's own scanner requirements page rates Google Pixel phones and Samsung Exynos phones 'not recommended' for phone scanning with the Otter and Ferret scanners. The same page asks for a Snapdragon 8 Gen 1+ or A15+ phone, says Intel Arc graphics cards are not supported, and lists Apple M2 or newer with macOS 14+ for Mac users. It also states that the Scan Bridge comes in separate Otter and Raptor/Sermoon versions.
standout_why: I compared against both cited Creality pages (the scanner-combo collection and the K2 Plus combo) and the top uncited results (3dprintmates.com, plus the rottenwifi.com and sekin.in titles). Neither Creality page states any OS, phone, GPU or bridge compatibility, and the combo pages don't even list what's in the box. 3dprintmates only says 'Up to 110fps on USB 3.0 computer' for the Pika and mentions an NVIDIA GPU for the POP 4. None of them name which phones or computers a scanner needs, what is excluded, or which bridge fits which scanner.
decides: This confirms the budget 'phone + Ferret SE + printer' route only for shoppers who have a Snapdragon 8 Gen 1+ Android phone or an A15+ iPhone (iPhone 13 or later). Pixel owners, Samsung Exynos owners, and PCs with Intel Arc graphics fall outside what Creality supports. That favors the Otter Lite, whose own page gives Windows/Mac requirements and puts its Lite Bridge in the box, over the standard Otter, which needs a $279 Scan Bridge (Otter version) for wireless scanning. Choosing between Creality's two printer-scanner bundles doesn't change, because neither combo page names the printer it includes.

findings.label: Android phones excluded for phone scanning
findings.value: Google Pixel series and Samsung Exynos models 'not recommended'; minimum Snapdragon 8 Gen 1+
findings.note: From the Phone Requirements table; page dated 2025-11-24. Minimum-supported examples given: Samsung S21/S22, Xiaomi 12, OPPO Find X5/X3, Vivo X90, Honor Magic 4/5. Raptor and Sermoon S1 need Snapdragon 8 Gen 3+.

findings.label: iPhone minimum for phone scanning
findings.note: The page contradicts itself: its 'minimum supported' example list includes iPhone 11 and 12, which have pre-A15 chips. The Otter Lite product page also says iPhone 13 (A15), iOS 15+, RAM ≥6 GB.

findings.label: GPU exclusion on Windows
findings.value: Intel Arc graphics cards 'not currently supported'
findings.note: Lowest supported Windows PC for Ferret/Otter: i5 8th Gen, 8 GB RAM, Creality Scan ≥ V2.3.0. Recommended: i7 12th Gen+, RTX 3060+, 16 GB+, Windows 10/11 64-bit.

findings.label: Mac requirement
findings.value: Apple M2/M3/M4, 16 GB+ RAM, macOS 14+; Intel Macs 'not recommended for high-end scanning'
findings.note: Raptor and Raptor Pro need M3/M4 with 32 GB+. This conflicts with the Otter Lite product page, which gives a Mac minimum of Intel i5-Gen8 with 8 GB and a recommendation of M1/M2/M3 with 16 GB.

findings.label: Wireless accessory and connection
findings.value: Lite Bridge included (Wi-Fi 6, 5 GHz, built-in battery); wired via USB-C to USB-A USB 3.0 cable; output OBJ/STL/PLY
findings.note: The box list includes the Lite Bridge, a 2 m USB 3.0 data cable, a 1.5 m USB 2.0 power cable, a turntable and a magnetic phone holder. Power is USB 3.0 5V 3A, or 12V 2A in Wi-Fi mode. The page says the standard Otter's wireless scanning needs 'wireless scanning accessories'.

findings.label: Android phone requirement (product page)
findings.note: Stricter than the compatibility blog's Snapdragon 8 Gen 1+ floor in one respect: the Snapdragon 888 is one generation older, so this page is actually more lenient. The two Creality documents differ.
